book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 20 · Trauma Systems and Mechanism of Injury
title: From Mechanism to Destination: Triage, Fluids and TXA

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already control bleeding, bind the pelvis, and move critical patients fast. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Predict injuries from bikes, pedestrians, falls, weapons and blasts
  2. Decide where and how fast: triage, platinum 10, BC Rapid Transport
  3. Resuscitate wisely: fluids, TXA and the lethal triad

Textbook: Chapter 20, PDF pages 1705–1737
slides.say: Welcome back. Last lesson you learned to read a vehicle crash and turn the mechanism into early decisions. Today we finish Chapter twenty. As an EMR you already control bleeding, bind the pelvis, and move critical patients quickly. As a PCP you add more judgment and more tools. First, we'll predict injuries from motorcycles, pedestrians, falls, knives, guns and explosions. Second, we'll decide where the patient goes and how fast. Third, resuscitation: what the book now says about fluids, the BC rules for TXA, and the lethal triad.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课你学会了读懂车祸，并把受伤机制变成早期决定。今天把第二十章讲完。作为 EMR，你已经会止血、固定骨盆、快速转运危重病人。作为 PCP，你要多一些判断，也多了工具。第一，预测摩托车、行人、坠落、刀伤、枪伤和爆炸造成的损伤。第二，决定病人送去哪里、多快送到。第三，复苏：书里现在怎么看补液，BC 对 TXA 的规定，以及致死三联征。

slides.title: Motorcycles and pedestrians
slides.body:
• Motorcycles: 2.8% of vehicles, 10.9% of road deaths (2016)
  • Helmet protects the head but passes force to the neck
  • Over the bars, feet on the pegs → both femurs or tibias
  • Fuel tank into the pelvis → open pelvic fracture; death rate near 50%
  • Adult pedestrian: bumper → legs; hood → head, chest, pelvis; then ground
  • Child: hit at pelvis or torso; often run over
slides.say: In 2016, motorcycles were under three percent of licensed vehicles in Canada but almost eleven percent of road deaths. A rider has no steel cage. The helmet protects the head but passes the force to the neck. In a head-on crash the rider goes over the handlebars, and feet caught on the pegs can break both femurs or both tibias. On some bikes the fuel tank wedges into the pelvis, and open pelvic fractures carry a death rate near fifty percent. For adult pedestrians, the bumper hits the legs, then the hood hits the head, chest and pelvis, then the ground. A child is hit higher, at the pelvis or torso, and is often run over.
slides.sayZh: 二零一六年，摩托车只占加拿大登记车辆的不到百分之三，却占道路死亡的将近百分之十一。骑手没有钢铁车厢保护。头盔保护头部，却把力量传到颈部。正面撞击时骑手会飞过车把，脚卡在踏板上可能造成双侧股骨或胫骨骨折。有些车型的油箱会像楔子一样插进骨盆，开放性骨盆骨折的死亡率接近百分之五十。成人行人被撞时，保险杠先撞腿，然后发动机盖撞到头、胸和骨盆，最后摔到地上。儿童被撞的位置更高，在骨盆或躯干，而且常被碾压。

slides.title: Falls from height
slides.body:
• Book triage: adult fall > 6 m; child > 3 m or 2–3× their height
  • Adult lands on feet: heels, legs → hip sockets, pelvis → lumbar spine
  • Lumbar fractures cluster around T12–L2
  • Liver, spleen and aorta decelerate; wrists break falling backward
  • Young children land head first
  • Surface: concrete and fast water barely give; deep snow does

A high fall is a major mechanism, not the simple fall BC excludes from binding.
slides.say: Falls are about height and landing. The textbook's triage guide flags adults who fall more than six metres, and children who fall more than three metres or two to three times their height. Adults often land on their feet, and the energy travels up: heels and legs, then the hip sockets and pelvis, then the lumbar spine, especially around T12 to L2. The liver, spleen and aorta decelerate hard, and the wrists break if they fall backward. Young children tend to land head first. The surface matters: concrete, and water at high speed, barely give. So a high fall is a major mechanism for the pelvis, unlike the simple fall that BC excludes from binding.
slides.sayZh: 坠落看两件事：高度和着地方式。教材的分诊指南把成人坠落超过六米、儿童坠落超过三米或身高的两到三倍列为警示。成人常常脚先着地，能量一路往上传：先是脚跟和腿，再到髋臼和骨盆，然后是腰椎，尤其是 T12 到 L2 附近。肝、脾和主动脉会剧烈减速；如果向后倒，手腕会骨折。幼儿往往头先着地。地面也有关系：水泥地，以及高速入水时的水面，几乎不会变形。所以高处坠落是骨盆的重大机制，不同于 BC 排除在骨盆固定之外的简单跌倒。

slides.title: Knives and guns: describe, don't label
slides.body:
• Stab: location, depth, blade length, angle
  • Low chest or upper belly: can enter both chest and abdomen
  • Guns: the tissue hit matters most
  • Liver, spleen, brain tear; lung, muscle, bowel stretch
  • Bullets bounce off bone; check armpits, buttock creases, skin folds
  • Describe location, size, shape: no “entry/exit”, no guessing the weapon
slides.say: With penetrating trauma, the wound you see tells you little about what's underneath. A stab wound's severity depends on the location, depth, blade length and angle. A wound in the lower chest or upper abdomen can enter both cavities, depending on where the diaphragm was at that moment. For gunshots, the tissue hit matters most. Lung, muscle and bowel stretch and recover better; liver, spleen and brain tear. Bullets don't always travel straight, so search the armpits, buttock creases and skin folds for more wounds. Document carefully: describe each wound's location, size and shape, but don't call it an entry or exit, and don't guess the weapon. Your report may end up in court.
slides.sayZh: 穿透伤的伤口外表，几乎说明不了里面伤成什么样。刀刺伤的严重程度取决于部位、深度、刀刃长度和角度。下胸部或上腹部的伤口可能同时进入胸腔和腹腔，取决于受伤那一刻膈肌的位置。枪伤最重要的是打到了什么组织：肺、肌肉、肠有弹性，恢复较好；肝、脾、脑会被撕裂。子弹不一定走直线，所以要检查腋窝、臀沟和皮肤皱褶里有没有别的伤口。记录要小心：描述每个伤口的位置、大小和形状，但不要写「入口」或「出口」，也不要猜凶器。你的报告可能会被用在法庭上。

slides.title: Blast injuries: ears point to lungs
slides.body:
TypeCause
Primarythe pressure wave itself
Secondaryflying debris and fragments
Tertiarybody thrown against objects
Quaternaryburns, toxic gas, crush
Quinaryadded biologic, chemical, radioactive material
  • Primary is the easiest to miss: ears, lungs, bowel
  • Ruptured eardrum → look for blast lung
slides.say: Explosions injure in five ways: the pressure wave itself, flying debris, the body being thrown, then burns, toxic gas and crush injuries, and finally biologic, chemical or radioactive material added to the bomb. The primary injury, from the pressure wave, is the easiest to miss, because it hits air-filled organs: the ears, lungs and bowel. The eardrum is the most sensitive, so a ruptured eardrum means look hard for blast lung: chest pain, coughing blood, fast breathing, or air under the skin. The book warns that positive pressure ventilation and IV fluids can make blast lung worse. And head injury is the most common cause of death after a blast.
slides.sayZh: 爆炸用五种方式伤人：冲击波本身；飞散的碎片；人被抛出撞击；烧伤、毒气和挤压伤；以及炸弹里额外加入的生物、化学或放射性物质。一级伤，也就是冲击波造成的伤，最容易漏诊，因为它打击含气的器官：耳朵、肺和肠道。鼓膜最敏感，所以鼓膜破裂就要仔细找爆炸肺：胸痛、咯血、呼吸急促，或皮下有气。书里提醒，正压通气和静脉补液都可能让爆炸肺更糟。爆炸后最常见的死因是颅脑损伤。

slides.q: After a workshop explosion, a man has ringing ears and blood in one ear canal. He says his breathing is fine; RR 24. What matters most?
options: It's an ear injury: dress the ear and treat him as non-urgent
Suspect blast lung and hidden injuries; watch his breathing and be careful with ventilation and fluids
Flush the ear canal with sterile saline
Do a needle decompression of the chest as a precaution
slides.say: Let's check. After a workshop explosion, a man has ringing ears and blood in one ear canal. He says his breathing is fine, and his respiratory rate is twenty-four. What matters most? A, it's an ear injury: dress the ear and treat him as non-urgent. B, suspect blast lung and other hidden injuries; watch his breathing closely, and be careful with ventilation and fluids. C, flush the ear canal with sterile saline. D, do a needle decompression of the chest as a precaution. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来检查一下。一间工坊发生爆炸后，一名男子耳鸣，一侧耳道有血。他说呼吸没问题，呼吸频率二十四。什么最重要？A 只是耳朵受伤：包扎耳朵，按非紧急处理；B 怀疑爆炸肺和其他隐匿伤，密切观察呼吸，通气和补液都要谨慎；C 用无菌生理盐水冲洗耳道；D 预防性地做胸腔针刺减压。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A ruptured eardrum tells you the pressure wave was strong enough to injure the lungs and bowel too, and his breathing rate is already up. A misses that warning. C treats the least important problem. D is wrong twice: there's no sign of tension, and needle decompression isn't in the BC chest trauma protocol on the licensing exam; BCEHS PCPs only do it after added-scope training.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。鼓膜破裂说明冲击波强到足以伤到肺和肠道，而且他的呼吸频率已经升高。A 忽略了这个警示。C 处理的是最不重要的问题。D 错了两次：没有张力性气胸的征象，而且 BC 执照考试的胸部创伤流程里没有针刺减压；BCEHS 的 PCP 要经扩展范围（Schedule 2）培训后才能做。

slides.title: Where to go: four triage steps
slides.body:
StepExamplesGo to
1 PhysiologyGCS ≤ 13, SBP < 90, RR < 10 or > 29highest-level trauma centre
2 Anatomypenetrating torso, flail chest, pelvic fracture, paralysishighest-level trauma centre
3 Mechanismadult fall > 6 m, ejection, motorcycle > 35 km/ha trauma centre
4 Specialolder adult, child, blood thinners, pregnancy > 20 wkconsider; local rules

Textbook guide: follow your regional destination rules. BC exam “unstable” mechanisms: fall > 6 m, major intrusion, ejection, a death in the vehicle, motorcycle or pedestrian/cyclist hit at > 30 km/h.
slides.say: Where should the patient go? The textbook uses a four-step field triage guide, adapted from US guidelines. Step one is physiology: a GCS of thirteen or less, a systolic under ninety, breathing under ten or over twenty-nine, or needing ventilation. Step two is anatomy, such as a penetrating wound to the torso, a flail chest, a pelvic fracture, or paralysis. Steps one and two go to the highest-level trauma centre. Step three is mechanism, like an adult fall over six metres, ejection, or a motorcycle crash over thirty-five kilometres an hour; that patient goes to a trauma centre. Step four covers special cases. Follow your regional destination rules. For the BC exam, though, the unstable list uses thirty kilometres an hour for motorcycles, pedestrians and cyclists.
slides.sayZh: 病人该送去哪里？教材用的是根据美国指南改编的四步现场分诊指南。第一步看生理：GCS 十三分或以下、收缩压低于九十、呼吸少于十次或多于二十九次，或需要通气支持。第二步看解剖：比如躯干穿透伤、连枷胸、骨盆骨折或瘫痪。第一、二步送最高级别的创伤中心。第三步看机制：比如成人坠落超过六米、被抛出车外，或时速超过三十五公里的摩托车事故；这类病人送创伤中心。第四步是特殊情况。按你所在地区的去向规定执行。不过在 BC 考试里，「不稳定病人」清单对摩托车、行人和骑车人用的是时速三十公里。

slides.title: Get moving: platinum 10 and Rapid Transport
slides.body:
Book: 10 min on scene. BC exam: unstable patient ready to load in 15 min

  • Book: on-scene “stabilizing” rarely helps; extricate and go
  • BC: every hip dislocation is Rapid Transport Category
  • BC: so is a hip fracture with nerve or blood-flow problems
  • BC: limb still pulseless after one realignment → unstable
  • BC: bind the pelvis before transport; IV and TXA en route

Air: long ground time, hard terrain, long extrication, or a critical procedure needed.
slides.say: Once you know the destination, move. The textbook calls it the platinum ten minutes: for a critical trauma patient, aim for no more than ten minutes on scene, unless extrication is difficult. On the BC practical exam, aim to have an unstable patient packaged and ready to load within fifteen minutes. In BC, the Rapid Transport Category marks a critical patient for rapid transport, and every hip dislocation is in it, as is a hip fracture with nerve or blood-flow problems. A limb that stays pulseless after one realignment attempt means managing the patient as unstable. Notice the BC pattern: bind the pelvis before you go, but the IV and TXA happen en route. Consider air transport when ground is too slow or can't get there.
slides.sayZh: 知道去向后，就要出发。教材叫它「白金十分钟」：危重创伤病人，现场停留不超过十分钟，解救困难的除外。在 BC 实操考试里，不稳定病人的目标是在十五分钟内完成评估、打包、可以上担架车。在 BC，快速转运类别（RTC）指需要快速转运的危重病人，所有髋关节脱位都属于这一类，伴有神经或血运问题的髋部骨折也是。肢体在一次复位尝试后仍然无脉，就要按不稳定病人处理。注意 BC 的规律：骨盆在出发前固定，静脉通路和 TXA 在途中做。地面转运太慢或到不了时，考虑空中转运。

slides.title: Fluids after trauma: less can be more
slides.body:
• Big early saline: raises BP, pops clots, dilutes clotting factors
  • Book: limiting field fluids in hypotensive trauma → better outcomes
  • Book: don't start an IV on scene just to give fluid
  • Saline is acidic; warm fluids to at least body temperature
  • BC: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • BC head injury: keep systolic > 120

Lethal triad: cold + poor clotting + acid. Stop bleeding, keep warm, go easy on saline.
slides.say: Now that you can give fluids, here's what the textbook says about trauma. Large amounts of early saline can raise the pressure, pop fresh clots and dilute clotting factors, so bleeding gets worse. Studies link limited field fluids with better outcomes in hypotensive trauma patients, and the book says don't start an IV on scene just to give fluid. This ties into the lethal triad: cold, poor clotting and acid. Saline is acidic, so keep the volume down, keep the patient warm, and warm the fluid to at least body temperature. The book also gives pressure targets, but on the BC exam use BC rules, including a systolic above one hundred twenty for a head injury.
slides.sayZh: 现在你能补液了，来看教材对创伤补液怎么说。早期大量输生理盐水，会让血压升高、冲掉新形成的血凝块、稀释凝血因子，出血反而更多。研究显示，对低血压的创伤病人，院前限制补液与更好的结局相关；书里还说，不要只为了补液在现场开静脉。这和致死三联征相连：冷、凝血差、酸。生理盐水偏酸，所以要少给，给病人保暖，并把液体加温到不低于正常体温。书里也给了血压目标，但 BC 考试要按 BC 规定，包括颅脑外伤时收缩压要高于一百二十。

slides.title: TXA: the BC checklist
slides.body:
BC drug monograph; Hypovolemia, Chest Trauma and Abdominal Injuries protocols

  • PCP only, given en route
  • Major trauma after starting the hypovolemia protocol
  • Or shock + MOI or exam suggesting hidden or ongoing bleeding
  • Not if: allergy, > 3 h since injury, age < 12, isolated TBI
  • Dose: 2 g (2000 mg) IV push over 1 minute

Pushed too fast → more hypotension.
slides.say: TXA, or tranexamic acid, helps the body form and keep blood clots. The textbook says it improved survival in combat, but routine paramedic use is still being studied. In BC, it's a PCP-only drug with clear criteria. Give it to a major trauma patient after you start the hypovolemia protocol, or to a patient with signs of shock when the mechanism or exam suggests hidden or ongoing bleeding. It appears in the hypovolemia, chest trauma and abdominal injury protocols. Hard stops: allergy, more than three hours since the injury, age under twelve, and an isolated head injury. The dose is two grams by IV push over one minute; faster can drop the pressure.
slides.sayZh: TXA，也就是氨甲环酸，帮助身体形成并维持血凝块。教材说它在战伤中提高了存活率，但救护员常规使用仍在研究中。在 BC，它是 PCP 专属药物，标准很明确。适用于已启动低血容量流程的重大创伤病人，或有休克征象、且受伤机制或体检提示隐匿或持续出血的病人。低血容量、胸部创伤和腹部损伤三个流程里都有它。硬性禁忌：过敏、受伤超过三小时、未满十二岁、单纯颅脑外伤。剂量是两克，静脉推注，一分钟推完；推得太快会让血压下降。

slides.q: Which patient meets the BC criteria for TXA?
options: A 10-year-old pedestrian in shock, hit 20 minutes ago
An adult with an isolated head injury, GCS 9, after a fall
An adult cyclist hit by a car 40 minutes ago: pale, HR 126, BP 84/50, unstable pelvis
An adult found in shock four hours after falling down the stairs
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. Which patient meets the BC criteria for TXA? A, a ten-year-old pedestrian in shock, hit twenty minutes ago. B, an adult with an isolated head injury and a GCS of nine, after a fall. C, an adult cyclist hit by a car forty minutes ago, pale, with a heart rate of one hundred twenty-six, a blood pressure of eighty-four over fifty, and an unstable pelvis. D, an adult found in shock four hours after falling down the stairs. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。哪位病人符合 BC 的 TXA 标准？A 一名十岁行人，二十分钟前被撞，处于休克；B 一名成人跌倒后单纯颅脑外伤，GCS 九分；C 一名成人骑车者，四十分钟前被车撞，面色苍白，心率一百二十六，血压八十四/五十，骨盆不稳定；D 一名成人从楼梯摔下，四小时后才被发现，处于休克。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. The cyclist has a major mechanism, signs of shock and a likely pelvic bleed, well within three hours. After you start the hypovolemia protocol, TXA fits: two grams IV push over one minute, en route. A is under twelve. B is an isolated head injury, which is a contraindication. D is past the three-hour limit.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。这名骑车者有重大受伤机制、休克征象，很可能有骨盆出血，而且远在三小时以内。启动低血容量流程后，符合 TXA 的使用：两克静脉推注，一分钟推完，在途中给。A 未满十二岁。B 是单纯颅脑外伤，属于禁忌。D 超过了三小时的时限。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: chest, abdomen and head
slides.body:
BC Chest Trauma, Abdominal Injuries and Traumatic Brain Injury protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Chest: three-sided seal; relieve it if tension develops
  • Chest: manually stabilize a flail segment
  • Abdomen: limit movement to protect clots; prevent heat loss
  • Head: SpO₂ ≥ 94%, head of bed 30°, loosen the collar

PCP adds

  • Chest, en route: vascular access if required; TXA if indicated
  • Abdomen, en route: IV, correct hypoperfusion; TXA if indicated
  • Head: glucose 4.0–8.0 mmol/L; systolic > 120
  • Head: IV to keep the vein open if systolic > 120; no TXA
slides.say: Penetrating and blunt trauma often lands in three BC protocols. On the left, every licence level. Chest: seal an open wound with a three-sided dressing or chest seal, relieve it if tension develops, and hold a flail segment by hand. Abdomen: limit movement so clots aren't disturbed, and prevent heat loss. Head injury: oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher, head of the bed at thirty degrees, and loosen the collar. On the right, the PCP adds, en route: vascular access and TXA when indicated for chest and abdomen. For a head injury: blood sugar four to eight, a systolic above one hundred twenty, and if it's already above that, the IV just keeps the vein open. And no TXA for an isolated head injury.
slides.sayZh: 穿透伤和钝性伤常常落在 BC 的三个流程里。左边是所有级别都做的。胸部：开放性伤口用三边封闭敷料或胸封贴封住，出现张力征象时放气，用手稳定连枷段。腹部：限制搬动以免扰动血凝块，防止热量流失。颅脑损伤：给氧使血氧达九十四以上，床头抬高三十度，松开颈托。右边是 PCP 增加的，在途中做：胸部和腹部伤建立静脉通路，符合指征时给 TXA。颅脑损伤：血糖维持在四到八，收缩压高于一百二十；如果已经高于一百二十，静脉通路只需保持通畅。单纯颅脑外伤不给 TXA。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Before TXA, ask when it happened: over 3 hours = no
  • Push TXA over a full minute; faster drops the BP
  • Isolated head injury: no TXA, and aim for systolic > 120
  • Blast lung: positive pressure and fluids can make it worse
  • Intoxicated patient: trust the mechanism over the complaint
  • Your new skills happen en route, not on scene
slides.say: Now the new watch-outs. One: before TXA, ask when the injury happened; past three hours, it's not given. Two: push TXA over a full minute; faster can drop the pressure. Three: an isolated head injury is the exception twice: no TXA, and a higher pressure target, above one hundred twenty. Four: after a blast, positive pressure ventilation and IV fluids can worsen blast lung, so go carefully and reassess often. Five: a patient on drugs or alcohol may not feel pain or protect an injury, so trust the mechanism more than the complaint. And six: the platinum ten minutes still applies. Your new skills happen in the ambulance, not on scene.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲新的注意事项。一，给 TXA 前先问受伤时间，超过三小时就不给。二，TXA 要推满一分钟，推太快会让血压下降。三，单纯颅脑外伤是双重例外：不给 TXA，而且血压目标更高，收缩压要高于一百二十。四，爆炸伤后，正压通气和静脉补液都可能加重爆炸肺，要谨慎、勤复评。五，吸毒或醉酒的病人可能感觉不到疼痛、不会护着伤处，所以要更相信受伤机制，而不是病人的主诉。六，白金十分钟依然适用：你的新技能在救护车上做，不在现场做。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Fluids: book at SBP < 70 → BC: bolus for SBP < 90 or poor perfusion
  • Head injury: book starts fluid at < 90 → BC: keep systolic > 120
  • TXA: book says unproven → BC: PCP drug with set criteria
  • Blast chest: book decompresses → BC exam: no needle decompression
  • Every hip dislocation: Rapid Transport Category
  • Sedation: benzodiazepines are not on the BC exam
slides.say: Here's where the book and BC differ. The book suggests starting crystalloid at a systolic under seventy in most trauma, or under ninety with a serious head injury. On the BC exam, use the BC protocols: consider a bolus for a systolic under ninety or poor perfusion, twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, and for a head injury, keep the systolic above one hundred twenty. The book calls routine TXA unproven; in BC it's a PCP drug with clear criteria. The book says blast injuries may need chest decompression; the BC exam protocols have none, though BCEHS PCPs may do it after added-scope training. Every hip dislocation is Rapid Transport. And the book mentions sedation for agitated patients, but benzodiazepines aren't on the BC licensing exam.
slides.sayZh: 这里是书和 BC 不一样的地方。书里建议，多数创伤在收缩压低于七十时开始输晶体液，疑似严重颅脑伤低于九十时开始。BC 考试要按 BC 流程：收缩压低于九十或灌注不良时考虑推注补液，每公斤二十毫升、最多两升；颅脑外伤收缩压要保持在一百二十以上。书里说常规使用 TXA 尚未证实；在 BC，它是有明确标准的 PCP 药物。书里说爆炸伤可能需要胸腔减压；BC 考纲流程里没有这项操作（BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围 Schedule 2 培训后可以做）。所有髋关节脱位都属于快速转运类别。书里提到给躁动病人镇静，但苯二氮卓类不在 BC 执照考试范围内。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Mechanism predicts injury: feet-first fall → heels, pelvis, lumbar spine; eardrum → lungs
  2. Go fast: platinum 10; pelvis bound first, IV and TXA en route
  3. TXA: 2 g IV over 1 min; not if > 3 h, age < 12, or isolated TBI

Next: Chapter 21, bleeding and shock
slides.say: Let's wrap up Chapter twenty. One: the mechanism predicts the injury. A feet-first fall means heels, pelvis and lumbar spine; a ruptured eardrum after a blast means look for the lungs; and a penetrating wound is described, never labelled. Two: go fast. Aim for ten minutes on scene with a critical patient, bind the pelvis before you leave, and do the IV and TXA en route. Three: TXA has BC rules: two grams by IV push over one minute, and never more than three hours after injury, under age twelve, or for an isolated head injury. Next, Chapter twenty-one: bleeding and shock. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 给第二十章收尾。一，受伤机制预测损伤：脚先着地的坠落，想到脚跟、骨盆和腰椎；爆炸后鼓膜破裂，去找肺的损伤；穿透伤只描述，不定性。二，要快：危重病人现场停留目标十分钟，出发前固定骨盆，静脉通路和 TXA 在途中做。三，TXA 有 BC 规定：两克静脉推注、一分钟推完；受伤超过三小时、未满十二岁、单纯颅脑外伤都不给。下一章，第二十一章：出血与休克。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
